# Thought Process: BFS Algorithm

#### Course: DSA with C++

## Thought Process: BFS Algorithm

To implement the BFS algorithm, we first need the following:

- A vector to store the sequence of traversal.
- An unordered set to keep track of the visited vertices.
- A queue to store the adjacent vertices of the current vertex.

```cpp
vector<int> traversal_seq;
unordered_set<int> visited;
queue<int> q;
q.push(start_vertex);
```

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

Now that we have everything we need, we'll start at start_vertex and follow the given steps to implement DFS in C++.

1. Dequeue the front element and make it the current vertex.

```cpp
int current_vertex = q.front();
q.pop();
```

2. Traverse the current vertex if it hasn't been traversed and add its neighbors to the queue.

This steps requires you to do the following:

- Add current_vertex to the traversal_seq vector.
- Add current_vertex to the visited set.
- Push the neighbors of current_vertex to the queue if they have not been visited.

```cpp
if (!visited.count(current_vertex)) {
    traversal_seq.push_back(current_vertex);
    visited.insert(current_vertex);

    for (auto neighbor : adj_list[current_vertex]) {
        if (!visited.count(neighbor)) {
            q.push(neighbor);
        }
    }
}
```

3. Repeat steps 1 and 2 as long as the queue is not empty.

```cpp
while (!q.empty()) {
    // Code of step 1 and 2
}
```

Now, we'll wrap all the code we've written inside the bfs_traversal() method, which will take start_vertex as an argument:

```cpp
vector<int> bfs_traversal(int start_vertex) {
    // Code from above steps
}
```
